statusText: Nine of the twenty-four published hours fall inside the CME equity-futures weekend halt and no United States macro release lands anywhere inside the window, holding Tail at the closed-venue floor. Every Friday primary mark re-verified unchanged this run. Two verified weekend items frame the restart in opposite directions: a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh was intercepted early Saturday with no casualties or damage, while crude closed Friday lower for a third consecutive session after China asked Iran to restrain the Houthis.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 5 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because the current hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. headline: An intercepted Riyadh missile and a third straight down day in crude pull the weekend ledger in opposite directions: the venue stays halted for nine of the 24 published hours and two-way discovery still frames the 22:00Z restart
body:
Nine of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME equity-futures weekend halt. The remaining fifteen contain the 22:00Z restart, the Asian session that follows and the European hours into Monday morning. Cash equities closed Friday 18 September and there has been no live NQ price path since 21:00Z that day.

Every Friday mark was re-verified at primary sources for this run and all are unchanged. The Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% against a previous close of 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 annual high. VIX closed 14.81, down 4.08%, near the low end of a 13.38-35.30 annual range. The H.15 release for 17 September prints the 2-year at 4.67%, the 10-year at 4.94% and the effective federal funds rate at 3.88%, the last confirming the 25 basis point hike delivered last week. Friday reporting put the 10-year near 5% after a further five basis point rise, with traders adding to bets on another hike in October. WTI settled 100.30 and Brent 103.87, both lower for a third consecutive session.

The internal composition of Friday's close argues against a trending regime rather than for one. Latest-session context shows semiconductor equipment up 4.85% and semiconductors up 1.87% while software-infrastructure fell 1.03% and communication services fell 0.74%; the eight largest Nasdaq constituents split four up and four down with a mean change of 0.24%. A narrow, rotational advance of that shape is poor raw material for the persistent no-retracement path that Tail measures.

Two verified weekend developments pull against each other. A Houthi ballistic missile fired at Riyadh at dawn on Saturday was intercepted and destroyed, with Saudi authorities reporting no casualties or damage, and a parallel attempt on an Aramco facility at Yanbu was reported thwarted; it was the first Riyadh air-raid alert since the July escalation, and no loss of export or production capacity has been confirmed. Against that, crude fell for a third session on Friday after China asked Iran to limit Houthi strikes on Saudi oil facilities and Riyadh worked to restore part of the damaged East-West pipeline. Hormuz remains constrained, with four commodity vessels transiting on Thursday against a ten-day average of sixteen. Conflicting inputs of this kind belong in the Stress channel rather than the Tail channel, and Stress is published at 31.

No United States macro release falls anywhere inside the published window. The Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday is the only scheduled US catalyst in it, and the week's first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs, followed by jobless claims and new home sales on Thursday and durable goods and final Michigan sentiment on Friday. A Trump-Xi summit is reported for Washington on Thursday with the tariff truce expiring 10 November as the market question; because no time is published and Beijing has not formally confirmed, it is held out of the verified event array and treated only as a week-ahead checkpoint. The rebalanced Nasdaq-100 weights take effect from Monday, with SpaceX rising to 2.82% from roughly 1.28%, but the rebalance trades executed at Friday's closing bell, so the change is a level effect rather than a fresh flow event at Monday's European open.

Tail holds 5 for the current hour and steps gradually through the remaining halt hours to 14, reaching a window high of 18 at the 22:00Z restart, where a weekend of unpriced headlines resolves into thin Sunday-evening liquidity. That step is a conditional gap allowance and not a reading of structure, since nothing can be classified until the reopen prints. The published path then decays through the Asian session, where Tokyo cash is shut for Japan's Respect-for-the-Aged holiday, and settles between 10 and 12 across the European hours into Monday midday. Every published hour maps to EA_ON, and no danger window is identified, because no observed persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullback sequence or failed-retracement evidence exists anywhere in the verified record. Dominant mode is normal for the halt and Asian hours and mixed for the restart and the Goolsbee window, where two-way conditional reaction is the reasonable framing.

Confidence is published at 76. Every primary level, yield, oil mark and calendar item was verified directly this run and the geopolitical and rebalance stories were confirmed at named publishers, which is close to complete evidence for what is knowable while the venue is closed. The offset is structural rather than a research gap: no live NQ price path exists for any provider during a weekend halt, and the shared cross-asset context file returned this run without its futures section, removing the delayed Treasury, crude and volatility futures read that would otherwise support the restart hours.

Stress opened at 22, drifted through 23 and 24 across Saturday afternoon and evening, stepped to 26 after midnight, eased to 25, then jumped to 29 at 05:00Z as the weekend escalation reporting landed and settled between 28 and 31 through the Sunday morning hours. Confidence ranged from 72 to 76 with no slot outside that band, reflecting a research record that stayed complete while the live-structure gap stayed open throughout.
